title: fuse-flow gate
description: What must hold before a step counts as done.

anyOf.description: The owner-action gate as a mapping: `owner-action: …`, optionally with `description` and `route_back_to`.

owner-action.description: The owner does what this text says, for example approve the design. Engine effect: the step waits for the owner (AWAITING_OWNER) when it is continued, until `fuse-flow continue <slug> --owner-approved`.

description.description: What the gate is for, in free text, for the reader. Engine effect: none.

route_back_to.description: The steps the work should go back to when this gate cannot be passed: one step id or a list, each this step or one before it. Usually the step that produces the artifact the gate finds fault with. Engine effect: when the step awaits the owner or is blocked, fuse-flow suggests these steps for `--back-to`, and the viewer draws them as routes back.

anyOf.description: The check gate as a mapping: `check: …`, optionally with `description` and `route_back_to`.

check.description: A kind of check, a single lower-case word such as `default`, which the project's policy binds to a command (checks: { default: bun run check }). Engine effect: the bound command runs from the repository root when the step is continued, and `continue` is refused unless it exits 0. An unbound kind refuses the step and tells the agent to find the command and record it; a kind bound to `none` passes.

anyOf.description: The script gate as a mapping: `script: …`, optionally with `description` and `route_back_to`.

script.description: A shell command, run from the repository root when the step is continued. Engine effect: `continue` is refused unless the command exits 0.

description.description: What the gate is for, in free text, for the reader. Engine effect: none.

anyOf.description: The agent gate as a mapping: `agent: …`, optionally with `max_rounds`, `guide`, `description` and `route_back_to`.

agent.description: What an independent agent reviews. The agent that did the work classifies each finding as a required fix (P0 or P1, unless the review guide says otherwise), optional (P2 or P3, fixed when cheap or deferred) or a false positive, fixes what is required, and they repeat until a round ends with no required fix, or as the review guide says; fixing optional findings after that round starts no further round. Engine effect: the text, the review guide and the round cap are printed with the step, and the agent that did the work counts the rounds; `continue` is refused until the reviewer has written a findings file in the step's current pass, unless the review was accepted or `--waived` records that the owner waived it.

description.description: What the gate is for, in free text, for the reader. Engine effect: none.

route_back_to.description: The steps the work should go back to when this gate cannot be passed: one step id or a list, each this step or one before it. Usually the step that produces the artifact the gate finds fault with. Engine effect: when the step awaits the owner or is blocked, fuse-flow suggests these steps for `--back-to`, and the viewer draws them as routes back.

max_rounds.description: How many review rounds that end with a required fix the step allows; 2 unless the workflow or policy says otherwise. When the cap is reached, the agent that did the work does not start another round; it runs `fuse-flow continue <slug> --blocked "<why>"`. Engine effect: none; fuse-flow prints the cap, raised by any rounds the owner granted, and does not count the rounds.

guide.description: A review guide for this gate, relative to the workflow file or absolute. It replaces the review guides of the step's artifacts and decides what counts as a required fix and when a round passes. A project's policy or its own library can replace it. Engine effect: printed with the step.

anyOf.description: The workflow gate as a mapping: `workflow: <name>`, optionally with `slug`, `for_each`, `inputs`, `returns`, `description` and `route_back_to`.

workflow.description: The workflow a child workstream follows, by name or by a path relative to this workflow file: the step waits for that procedure. Engine effect: when the step is handed out, fuse-flow creates the child workstream with its inputs bound from this workstream's documents, and `continue` is refused until the child is complete. After a send-back, the next pass gets a fresh child. With `for_each: <folder artifact>`, the step waits for one child per file of that folder, each given its own file, and `continue` is refused until every child is complete.

slug.description: The child workstream's slug, a template that contains {slug}, the parent's slug, and something more, and may contain {step}, this step's id; {slug}-{step} unless set. With for_each it must also contain {item}, the item's id; {slug}-{step}-{item} unless set. Engine effect: the child is created under this slug; a later pass of the step after a send-back adds -<pass>, such as -2.

for_each.description: A folder artifact of this workflow, available before this step, whose direct files are the items: the step waits for one child workstream per file, the item's id being the file name without its extension. Engine effect: when the step is handed out, fuse-flow records the set of items and creates one child per item, binding every input that names this artifact to the item's own file; `continue` is refused until every child is complete, and later steps read what each child returned, one document per item.

inputs.description: The documents the child is given: child input id -> artifact id in this workflow, available before this step. Engine effect: each binds the child's declared input to this workstream's document; with for_each, an input that names the for_each artifact is bound to the item's file.

returns.description: The child's documents later steps of this workflow may consume: a list of ids, or a mapping of id in this workflow -> id in the child, to rename one. Engine effect: a later step's `consumes` resolves each to the newest child's recorded document, or with for_each to one document per child.
